population: Adult runners (18+). This is a product applicability boundary, not an age field, inference or validation requirement.
application_boundary: Use only this fixed approved knowledge for material coaching recommendations. No fallback to unapproved LLM training knowledge or runtime research.
Provide useful general direction and priorities for the next recommendation week, not a Training Plan.
Do not prescribe day-by-day schedules, exact workouts, distances, durations, paces, heart-rate zones, interval structures, numeric progression targets, multiweek plans or race-time predictions.
Distinguish Strava-observed records, deterministic derivations, attributed RunnerContext and approved knowledge. Name-based TrainingType classifications are not measured intensity or readiness.

Missing or uncertain prerequisites require withholding the affected recommendation or focused clarification; other independently supported partial guidance may remain available. An if-appropriate qualifier must not conceal a missing prerequisite.
Health-related context may influence caution, but must not become diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation advice or medical clearance. Do not resolve source differences through invented rules.

sources.title: Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, second edition
sources.author: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
sources.locator: Chapter 6; Increase Physical Activity Gradually Over Time; printed page 90
sources.supporting_guidance: Reviewed paraphrase: increase activity gradually toward goals, with individualization informed by fitness and experience.
sources.knowledge_basis: Evidence-informed public-health organizational guidance; not a running-specific return prescription.
review_notes: The relevant passage was reviewed through indexed extraction; full PDF retrieval failed during the approved research.
Detailed inactive-person guidance is not automatically applicable to an experienced runner after vacation. Numeric recommendations are not adopted.

sources.title: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour
sources.author: World Health Organization
sources.supporting_guidance: Reviewed paraphrase: start with small amounts of physical activity and increase gradually.
sources.knowledge_basis: Organizational good-practice statement, distinguished from formally graded recommendations.
review_notes: Relevant text was reviewed through indexed recommendations and the executive summary.
Broad adult physical-activity guidance corroborates the principle, not a running-specific return dose or timeline.

sources.title: How to Overcome the Reversibility Principle and Help Your Clients Get Back on Track
sources.author: ACE Certified publication; reviewed expert article
sources.locator: The All-Important Why?; Taking an Individualized Approach; Type of Exercise; conclusion
sources.supporting_guidance: Reviewed paraphrase: consider the reason for the break and previous training; begin cardiorespiratory exercise slowly rather than immediately restoring previous demands. Research on optimal return strategies is limited.
sources.knowledge_basis: Return-specific expert interpretation published by an exercise-professional organization, not a formal consensus guideline or controlled return-strategy comparison.
review_notes: Stronger assertions about inevitable injury or specific fitness loss are not adopted.
Supports individualized resumption; does not supply V1 running-day counts, workout categories or progression formulas.

sources.title: Road to Health Toolkit: Activities Guide
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.locator: Appendix; Be Active, Be Safe; printed page 29 (PDF page 33)
sources.supporting_guidance: Reviewed paraphrase: slow or stop activity when very tired or when joints hurt; its restart example concerns an illness-related break.
sources.knowledge_basis: Community-health education for diabetes prevention; applicability caution, not individualized running or vacation-return guidance.
review_notes: Activity-time caution must not become a general weekly fatigue prescription.
Illness-specific restart advice and surrounding medical advice are not adopted as a Coach medical layer.

sources.title: Simplifying the running jargon: Training pace
sources.author: England Athletics; Tom Craggs, National Endurance Manager
sources.locator: Easy vs. steady state running; Which is more beneficial for training?
sources.supporting_guidance: Reviewed paraphrase: easy running is relaxed and fully conversational; keep intended easy running relaxed rather than drifting into harder steady running.
sources.knowledge_basis: Named expert organizational running guidance in an educational interview, not a systematic review or tested weekly decision rule.
review_notes: Comfortable conversation is a qualitative prospective description, not a physiological threshold.
Steady running may permit more effortful conversation; that must not dilute the approved relaxed, comfortable full-conversation description.

sources.title: Education for Runners
sources.author: Road Runners Club of America
sources.locator: Managing Aches and Pains; Train, don't strain
sources.supporting_guidance: Reviewed paraphrase: running need not be all-out to provide benefits; conversation is a practical guide to effort.
sources.knowledge_basis: Organizational guidance principally for beginners; no individualized weekly distribution rule.
review_notes: Publication/revision date and underlying evidence are not clearly documented.
Surrounding medical advice, frequency prescriptions and other numerical recommendations are not imported.

sources.title: How to Get Started Running in the New Year
sources.author: NYRR Staff; New York Road Runners
sources.locator: Introduction; How Far, How Fast, How Often
sources.supporting_guidance: Reviewed paraphrase: addresses new and returning runners and describes easy running through the ability to speak in sentences.
sources.knowledge_basis: Practical organizational guidance for recreational beginners and returners, not a tested prescription for established runners.
review_notes: Only qualitative effort guidance is adopted. No session frequency or detailed execution advice is adopted.
Its conversational description is less detailed than England Athletics; the package retains comfortable full conversation without equating these descriptions to measured intensity.

sources.title: The perfect way to return to running
sources.author: England Athletics; no named author in the reviewed record
sources.supporting_guidance: Reviewed paraphrase: a gradual comeback at lower demands includes easy running as an initial component.
sources.knowledge_basis: Supplementary organizational return guidance without a named author or traceable supporting studies.
review_notes: Categorical claims about fitness loss and damage are not adopted.
This supplementary passage does not independently authorize an interruption rationale; use the separately approved return item and its prerequisites.

actionable_items.guidance: When a recent qualifying recorded episode is accompanied by RunnerContext confirming an actual training interruption and resumption, recommend a gradual, individualized resumption. Previous recorded volume may explain history, but is not current capacity, an immediate target or something that must eventually be recovered.
actionable_items.knowledge_basis: Bounded synthesis of organizational gradual-progression good practice and return-specific expert interpretation; not a validated running return formula. Prerequisites are product application restrictions, not a source-derived physiological threshold.
prerequisites: Adult-runner product scope applies without collecting or inferring age.
A recent qualifying ObservedRunningAfterZeroRunWeeks result under the approved Coach history contract.
Original RunnerContext clearly confirms an actual training interruption and subsequent resumption corresponding to that recorded episode.
Recent evidence satisfies the approved history/applicability boundary; unresolved reported circumstances must not be concealed by generic return advice.
Any statements about previous recorded volume reference actual supplied pre-interruption background observations.
permitted_conclusions: Recommend gradual individualized resumption as a non-numeric next-week direction.
Advise against making immediate restoration of pre-interruption volume the objective.
Explain supplied previous weekly volume as historical context, distinct from current observations and capacity.
Apply the gradual-return principle without historical background, while omitting discussion of unknown previous volume.
limitations_exceptions: The Insight alone establishes only consecutive supplied zero-Run observations followed by observed Run activity, not actual inactivity, rest, interruption, resumption or detraining.
Resume progressively does not mean increase next week. No amount, rate, deadline, rebuilding timeline or requirement to recover old volume is supported.
No running-day count, numeric frequency reduction, quality-work recommendation, longer-run recommendation or exact volume is supported.
No fitness-loss estimate, race readiness, injury prediction or medical safety conclusion is supported.
Missing background does not invalidate gradual resumption; it prevents claims about previous recorded volume.
Do not use this item as injury rehabilitation, illness-return medical advice or clearance to continue despite discomfort or conflicting treatment advice.
Fatigue, poor sleep and stress remain attributed context, not a basis for invented physiology, weekly prescriptions or therapeutic claims.
Race proximity does not justify accelerated rebuilding. Historical volume is never an immediate target or a mandatory eventual recovery objective.
reviewed_conflicts_differences: HHS and WHO address broad physical activity; ACE addresses returning exercisers; CDC's explicit restart example concerns illness. They do not share a runner-specific dose or prerequisite checklist.
The detector's at-least-two-zero-week definition is a recorded-pattern rule, not an evidence-derived physiological threshold.
Stronger source claims about injury or fitness loss are excluded. No reviewed difference is resolved by adopting an invented numerical compromise.

actionable_items.guidance: For an adult runner undertaking running training, the Coach may recommend making relaxed, conversational running a priority in the following week and keeping intended easy running genuinely easy. Easy means relaxed effort at which comfortable full conversation is possible.
actionable_items.knowledge_basis: Expert and organizational running guidance supports a qualitative definition and general training component. Application to the following week is a bounded product interpretation, not evidence of optimal weekly structure for every runner.
prerequisites: Adult-runner product scope applies without collecting or inferring age.
Current running or resumption is established by recent supplied evidence or an explicit attributed user report.
Availability permits running in the recommendation week.
Supplied circumstances do not leave applicability of running guidance materially unresolved; no affirmative medical clearance or new health questionnaire is implied.
An interruption-specific rationale additionally requires TK_RETURN_AFTER_REPORTED_INTERRUPTION@1.0.0 and its qualifying evidence plus RunnerContext confirmation.
permitted_conclusions: Recommend qualitative attention to relaxed, conversational running as a general training component, without inventing an individual deficit.
Describe prospective easy effort through comfortable full conversation and keeping intended easy running relaxed.
Use a confirmed interruption as an additional rationale only through the separately approved return item.
limitations_exceptions: Easy is not a pace, heart-rate zone, measured physiological intensity or verified description of previous runs.
Priority does not prescribe a weekly percentage, an exclusively easy week, running-day counts or easy-session counts.
No quality-work inclusion/exclusion, total-load direction, longer-run structure, progression, taper, race readiness or medical safety conclusion is supported.
TrainingType.EASY counts are name-based labels, not measured easy effort. Zero EASY labels do not establish absence of easy running.
Increasing, decreasing or stable distance and persistent distance Insights do not automatically change applicability or establish a recovery need.
Historical volume does not set easy-running volume or prove current capacity.

Discomfort, illness, fatigue, poor sleep or stress do not establish that easy running is safe, therapeutic or preferable to rest. Withhold affected guidance or clarify material uncertainty rather than saying just run easy.
Race proximity does not turn this general priority into taper, race execution or catch-up training guidance.
reviewed_conflicts_differences: England Athletics distinguishes comfortable conversation from more effortful conversation during steady running; RRCA and NYRR use less detailed conversational descriptions. Retain relaxed comfortable full conversation without claiming a shared scientific threshold.
Sources address established runners, beginners and returners differently. The return-specific passage supplies supplementary context only through the approved return item's prerequisites.

These sources are expert/organizational guidance, not direct research establishing an optimal next-week distribution. Numerical prescriptions and categorical fitness-loss or damage claims are excluded.

statements: PersistentWeeklyRunningDistanceIncrease establishes three strict weekly distance increases across four qualifying observations; interpret recorded evolution factually.
The pattern does not establish excessive, beneficial, dangerous or physiologically significant progression, improved fitness, inadequate recovery or injury risk.
The pattern does not justify maintaining, reducing or continuing progression next week. Maintain is not an unsupported neutral/default prescription.
Magnitude remains visible through observations and Trends, but no approved threshold converts it into a coaching recommendation.
Other independently approved knowledge may support guidance when this Insight is present. No pattern-based maintain/reduce item is approved.
General training value does not establish that a specific runner should include, limit or avoid quality-oriented work next week.
No approved V1 item supports quality inclusion, exclusion, deferral, a specific session count or an at-most-one limit.
TrainingType.TEMPO and TrainingType.INTERVALS are name-based classifications, not verified physiological intensity, execution or readiness; missing labels do not prove missing quality work.
Recent history, confirmed interruption, target-date proximity and user reports do not supply an approved quality-readiness rule.
The return and easy-priority items do not authorize quality decisions. Withholding unsupported guidance is distinct from recommending avoidance.
Longer runs are recognized components of half-marathon preparation in general, but this does not establish next-week inclusion for a specific runner.
Half-marathon goal and target-date proximity alone do not justify a relatively longer run.
Weekly totals, activity counts, Trends and Insights do not establish individual-run distribution or longer-run readiness.
TrainingType.LONG is name-based, not actual longest-run exposure, magnitude, effort or tolerance. Absence of LONG labels does not prove absence of relatively longer runs.
Historical weekly volume is not current single-run capacity; confirmed interruption is not longer-run readiness; easy effort does not make longer running appropriate or safe.
Withholding unsupported inclusion differs from advising avoidance. No exact distance, duration, percentage, progression or eligibility threshold is approved.
recommended_running_days remains optional and must be unspecified when no approved knowledge supports a count. This package contains no specific-count item.
available_training_days_per_week is strictly a maximum constraint, not recommended use. No use-all-days, availability-minus-one or other default heuristic is approved.
running_activity_count counts activities, not distinct running days. Historical activity counts or Trends must not be interpreted as running-day frequency.
A user-reported familiar running frequency is attributed context, not automatically a recommendation; clipping it to availability does not establish appropriateness.
The return item does not justify numeric frequency reduction, and the easy-priority item does not justify any running-day or session count.
Race proximity, stress, sleep, fatigue and discomfort do not independently justify inventing a count.
Zero availability is a hard structural constraint: no positive running-day recommendation is permitted. An unspecified count must not be replaced by an implied count in prose.
